title: Micro-benchmark journal — local latency experiments
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal tracker for small runs I do on local/dev clusters to triage latency regressions and batching effects. Not exhaustive — notes-to-self + mini-table for copy/paste into tickets or slack.

How I use this:
- Run a small series (3-5 seeds) for each knob change (batch size, kv cache, quant profile).
- Collect p50/p95, throughput (tok/s), and anecdata (spikes, stalls).
- Paste the best run into PR description or INF ticket, link this doc.

Summary of latest investigations (high level):
- Observed a ~15% p95 regression when enabling new kernel for attention in fp16 with long sequences (>512) on A10G.
- KV-cache prefix caching reduced tokens processed by ~30% for repeated prompt workloads but added ~4ms overhead on cold-starts.
- 4-bit quant config q4f should be tested with cache disabled (weird desync observed).

Mini table (CSV-style for quick copying):
date,model,gpu,batch,seq,quant,p50_ms,p95_ms,throughput_tok_s,notes,commit
2024-11-09,llama-2-7b,a10g,1,128,fp16,38,185,160,"baseline local; default kernels",abc1234
2024-11-10,llama-2-7b,a10g,4,128,fp16,55,270,520,"batching ups throughput, p95 worse under tail load",abc1234
2024-11-12,llama-2-7b,a10g,1,1024,fp16,150,780,42,"long seq regression after kernel swap",def5678
2024-11-15,llama-2-7b,a10g,1,512,q4f,62,320,140,"q4f + caching flaky (desync), lower throughput expected",fed9a10
2024-11-28,redwood-compat-3b,a10g,8,128,fp16,25,110,1100,"dedicated config check; autoscale off",a1b2c3d

Quick experiment notes (free-text):
- 2024-11-12 run: p95 spikes correlated with GC on the process — need a profiling run with pprof. Suspect large allocations when KV cache grows.
- Cold start vs warm: measure cold by restarting process between each sample; warm means continuous run with random prompt set. Warm wins heavily for throughput but hides cold-start regressions developers see in canaries.
- Batching policy: current 'adaptive' policy reduces p50 by 10% in stable load but p95 suffers when load is bursty. Try 'fixed-3' policy for stability experiments.

How to reproduce (notes-to-self):
- Script: infra/bench/run_local_bench.sh --model llama-2-7b --gpu a10g --batch 1 --seq 512 --quant fp16 --steps 100 --out /tmp/bench.out
- Use bench_viz.py to extract p50/p95 and tok/s. Commit used: def5678 for kernel swap tests.

Data collection checklist (so I don't forget fields):
- [ ] model name + exact checkpoint/hash
- [ ] hardware (GPU model + driver + CUDA/cuDNN)
- [ ] batch size, sequence length, tokenization settings
- [ ] quantization profile (if any) and conversion script
- [ ] profiling artifacts (pprof, nvprof) attached or linked
- [ ] seed/replicate info and whether run was cold or warm

Open questions / TODOs: 
- TODO: run a profile for the 2024-11-12 long-seq case with --trace-alloc and collect pprof.
- TODO: test q4f with cache disabled + compare distributions of token time to detect desync.
- Q: Could the kernel selection heuristics be choosing an fp32 fallback path for long sequences? Check runtime logs for 'fallback' messages.

Slack snippet (copy-paste ready):
"Heads up: small local bench shows ~15% p95 regression on long-seq after kernel swap (runs 2024-11-12, commit def5678). Repro steps and logs in micro-bench-journal (users). Suggesting a profiling run and temporary rollback until root cause identified. cc @aisha @ethan"

References / quick links: 
- PR for kernel swap: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/88
- Ticket tracking perf regression: JIRA:INF-237
- Local bench scripts: repo:infra/bench/README.md

Notes to future me: keep the CSV rows minimal; if a run becomes important, promote to a proper Drive doc in shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/benchmarks with full artifacts attached.

-- Leah
